newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greece will protect Cyprus from Turkey - minister.
newsitem.headline: Greece will protect Cyprus from Turkey - minister.

text.p: Greek Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos started a four-day official visit to Cyprus on Thursday with a pledge Greece will protect the island until a political settlement is found to its division.
"I can guarantee to you we will fortify Cyprus because this is an obligation and a command for all of us," Tsohatzopoulos told reporters soon after arriving in Cyprus on a military aircraft.

The Greek minister is due to have meetings with his Cypriot counterpart Costas Eliades on present and future defence planning. He is also due to meet Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides and military officials.
Under a defence pact agreed between the two countries in 1993, Greece will come to Cyprus's aid in the event of fresh hostilities with Turkey on the divided island.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded its north in 1974, sparked by a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling Greece at the time.
Turkey, which has 30,000 troops stationed in northern Cyprus, in 1983 declared a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state but it is recognised only by Ankara.

Tsohatzopoulos said the defence pact and the accession negotiations Cyprus is due to start with the European Union in early 1998 were the impetus making a settlement to the issue "The creation of the unified defence area (under the defence pact) is really the political response of hellenism against the expansionism and threat of Turkey" said Tsohatzopoulos.
He did not answer any questions.

Tensions on the island have been running high since two Greek Cypriots were killed in ceasefire line protests in August, a Turkish Cypriot sentry was found shot dead at his ceasefire line post and a retired Greek Cypriot fireman was shot dead by when he strayed into Turkish held areas.
